sentences.text:
Heard Sri Arjun Kumar Kaushal, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Vishwanath Nishad,
learned Aga for the State and Sri Brij Bhushan Singh, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 as
well as perused the record.

2.  This Court has passed the order dated 21.02.2024 which reads as under:
"1. Heard Sri Arjun Kumar Kaushal, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Nirmal Pandey, learned AGA for the State as well as Sri Brij Bhushan Singh, Advocate who has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party no. 2.
His Vakalatnama is taken on record.

2. This petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner with the Maneesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34660086/
1 prayer to quash the entire proceedings of S.T. No. 1240 of 2020; State Vs. Maneesh Kumar, arising out of Case Crime No. 271 of 2020, under Section 376, 498-A, 323,
504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Kachauna, District Hardoi, pending before the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, Hardoi, on the basis that the petitioner and the complainant have got married and are living as husband and wife with their 3 years old daughter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. Today, Maneesh Kumar, the petitioner and opposite party no. 2,
complainant/victim, who is wife of the petitioner, are present in person with their minor daughter aged about 3 years and 4 months.
Both the parties have stated that they are living together happily as husband and wife alongwith their minor daughter.
The opposite party no. 2 has stated that she has no grievance against her husband Maneesh Kumar as he is properly looking after her and her minor daughter.

4. On being confronted as to whether they got their marriage registered before the Registrar, Marriages, both have stated that they have not registered their marriage before the Registrar, Marriages till date.
5. Learned counsel for the parties have stated that some short time may be given to them to get their marriage registered before the aforesaid authority.
6. On the aforesaid request, the case is adjourned for today.

The liberty is given to the petitioner and opposite party no. 2 to get their marriage registered before the Registrar, Marriages within a period of three weeks from today and marriage registration certificate may be filed on the next date by filing supplementary affidavit.
The Registrar, Marriages shall do the needful with expedition as soon as the aforesaid parties apply for marriage registration.

7. On the next date, the parties, who are present today, need not appear again,
however, learned counsel for the parties may file the affidavits.

8. When the case is listed next, name of Sri Brij Bhushan Singh be printed in the cause list as learned counsel for opposite party no. 2.
9.
List this case on 14.03.2024, within top ten cases.
10. Till the next date of listing, further proceedings of S.T. No. 1240 of 2020 shall remain stayed."
3. Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 has filed supplementary affidavit, the same is taken on record.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn attention of this Court towards Annexure No. SA-2 to the supplementary affidavit dated 04.03.2024 which has earlier been filed enclosing therewith Maneesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: the marriage certificate of the petitioner Maneesh Kumar and opposite party no. 2, Anuradha Devi dated 29.02.2024.

Since the petitioner and opposite opposite party no. 2 are living happily as husband and wife with their minor children and they have no grievance against each other, then there is no purpose to keep this petition pending any longer.
Further, opposite party no. 2 in her statement has stated that her husband is looking after her and her minor children properly.

5. Sri Vishwanath Nishad, learned AGA has also not disputed the aforesaid facts that the petitioner and opposite party no. 2 are living together happily as husband and wife with their minor children and they do not wish to litigate each other and opposite party no. 2 has herself requested that the criminal case against her husband may be set aside.
6.

The Apex Court in re: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343 has observed that even if the offence(s) in question is/are not compoundable within the scope of section 320 Cr.P.C. even then considering the facts and circumstances of the case in question the Constitutional Court may allow the parties to compound such offence(s) on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

7. Not only the above, considering the facts and circumstances of the issue in question and other dictums of Hon'ble Apex Court in re: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; 2003 (4) SCC 675, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303; State of Rajasthan vs. Shambhu Kewat, (2014) 4 SCC 149; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Deepak (2014) 10 SCC 285; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Manish (2015) 8 SCC 307; J.Ramesh Kamath vs. Mohana Kurup (2016) 12 SCC 179;
State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Rajveer Singh (2016) 12 SCC 471; Parbatbhai AAhir vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641 the entire proceedings of the aforesaid S.T. No. 1240 of 2020 are hereby quashed.
